q: Which zone should hold critical internal databases rather than public-facing servers or guest clients?
exp: The guide separates critical servers into a private security zone and exposes only necessary services in a perimeter or public server zone.

q: In a screened subnet, what does the external filtering boundary separate?
opts: The perimeter network from the private LAN
The internet from the perimeter network
exp: The outside boundary filters traffic between the untrusted internet and the perimeter network; a second boundary protects the private LAN.

q: A public web server needs a back-end database. Where should the database remain?
opts: On the same unfiltered public segment
In a private zone behind an internal filtering boundary
exp: Only specific necessary connections should cross from the public-facing server zone to a protected internal database.

q: What is SCADA used for in an industrial environment?
opts: Supervising and acquiring data from distributed processes
exp: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems monitor and control industrial conditions using operational data.

q: Why might a low-power sensor network require an IoT gateway?
opts: Its devices may use a protocol that needs bridging to IP
A gateway removes the need for authentication
It turns a private zone into a public zone
exp: A gateway connects constrained sensor networks to ordinary IP services while their access still needs protection.

q: Which cellular technology is suited to small, low-power IoT messages?
exp: Narrowband IoT targets constrained devices that send relatively small amounts of data.

q: Compared with NB-IoT, what kind of device demand generally fits LTE-M better?
exp: The guide contrasts narrowband sensor messaging with LTE-M applications that need more data capacity.

q: Why should an IT-to-OT connection have tightly limited access and careful change control?
opts: A compromise could affect physical process availability or safety
exp: Operational technology can control real equipment; availability and safety can matter more than rapid software changes.

q: Which camera type can pan, tilt, and zoom to follow movement across a wider area?
exp: A PTZ camera can move its field of view; a fixed camera observes a set area.

q: What can PoE provide to a compatible IP camera over its Ethernet cable?
exp: Power over Ethernet can supply a compatible network camera while the same cable carries its data.

q: Which management system can apply a location-based restriction to a managed phone?
exp: Mobile device management can use geofencing as a policy condition, though location readings may be imprecise.

q: Why pair a locked server rack with cameras in a shared facility?
opts: A rack lock replaces storage encryption
The lock restricts access while cameras record and alert
exp: These controls serve different purposes: prevention at the rack and observation or evidence from surveillance.

q: Which satellite orbit generally adds more propagation delay to a remote internet link?
exp: Geostationary satellites are much farther from Earth than low-Earth-orbit satellites, increasing signal travel time.

q: A site uses GPS for location. What does this prove about its internet connection?
opts: Nothing; positioning and satellite broadband are different services
exp: GPS/GNSS provides positioning signals and does not imply that the site has satellite internet access.

q: A client has good RSSI but poor SNR. Which condition should you investigate?
opts: Noise or interference near the client
A lack of any received signal
exp: RSSI describes received signal strength; SNR compares the useful signal with background noise.

q: Which site survey associates a test client with the WLAN to measure actual connectivity?
exp: An active survey joins the WLAN and tests service; a passive survey listens, while a predictive survey models coverage.

q: Which survey type models expected Wi-Fi coverage before access points are installed?
exp: A predictive survey estimates RF coverage from building and AP inputs and should be validated after deployment.

q: Three APs broadcast one SSID. What identifies one specific AP radio?
exp: The BSSID identifies a basic service set, typically using an AP radio MAC; the SSID can be shared across APs.

q: What should replace hidden-SSID settings as the primary way to protect a WLAN?
opts: A shared guest VLAN with servers
exp: Beacons advertise WLAN information; suppressing the SSID name is not a meaningful security control.

q: What is an important tradeoff when WDS or repeating connects APs wirelessly?
exp: Wireless links between APs use finite airtime and require compatible, secure configuration.

q: A client remains attached to a distant weak AP even though a stronger AP is nearby. What is this called?
exp: A sticky client delays roaming to a better AP; supported 802.11k/v/r features may help roaming behavior.

q: Which antenna type better suits a focused building-to-building wireless bridge?
exp: A directional antenna concentrates its pattern toward a particular target rather than covering a room broadly.

q: Which authentication method does WPA3-Personal use?
exp: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals improves password-based Wi-Fi authentication resistance to offline guessing.

q: Which EAP method commonly uses client and server certificates for enterprise WLAN authentication?
exp: EAP-TLS uses certificates with 802.1X and a back-end authentication service such as RADIUS.

q: What does a captive portal fail to provide by itself on an open guest WLAN?
exp: A portal is an access workflow, not a link-layer encryption protocol.

q: Which feature helps protect clients from forged Wi-Fi deauthentication frames?
exp: PMF protects selected management frames and helps reduce spoofed deauthentication or disassociation attacks.

q: Which tool can reveal radio interference that does not appear as Wi-Fi frames?
exp: A spectrum analyzer shows RF energy from Wi-Fi and non-Wi-Fi sources such as appliances or other radio devices.

q: A dense WLAN has strong signal but poor performance from airtime contention. Which change can help channel reuse?
opts: Set every AP to maximum width and power
Use narrower channels with a planned AP layout
exp: Narrower channels and deliberate reuse can reduce contention; capacity planning also considers simultaneous clients.
